samples.summary: Toggle-off clears `underline`/`strikethrough` but leaves the companion keys `underlineStyle`, `underlineColor`, `strikeStyle`, so the run still cannot re-merge
samples.evidence: `BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS` covers only bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/superscript/subscript. `inlineStylesEqual` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:404-412) also compares `underlineStyle`, `underlineColor` and `strikeStyle`. A run that carries `underlineStyle: 'double'` (produced by DOCX/PPTX import — packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts, and copied by the format painter which enumerates the key at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2837) keeps that orphan key after Cmd+U turns underline off, so `normalizeInlines` still refuses to merge it with its neighbour — exactly the split-forever symptom the change claims to remove, and a dead key that also has no rendering meaning once `underline` is gone.

samples.summary: On the production Yorkie path the CRDT tree keeps the split inline nodes after the clear, so the re-merge the change is built around only holds in the in-memory cache and is lost on reload
samples.evidence: `applyStyleInTree` splits inline nodes, styles/removes attributes (lines 1884-1889) and only deletes *empty* inlines (Step 6, lines 1892-1904); nothing ever coalesces two adjacent inline nodes with now-identical attributes. The block cache is updated with `applyInlineStyleHelper` (line 1770), which *does* call `normalizeInlines`, so the running session shows one run while the Tree holds three. `treeNodeToBlock` (line 418-426) performs no merge either, so after a reload/rejoin the block comes back split again. The new docs test asserting `inlines).toHaveLength(1)` only exercises MemDocStore, so nothing detects this divergence.

samples.summary: Every B/I/U/S toggle-off now emits a `removeStyleByPath` op instead of a `styleByPath` set; concurrent-edit resolution between remove-attribute and set-attribute ops is not the same LWW path the old `bold=false` write used
samples.evidence: The comment added at lines 1871-1881 only reasons about undo. The change moves the hottest editing path from `styleByPath({bold:'false'})` to `styleByPath(existing) + removeStyleByPath(['bold'])`. If Yorkie resolves a concurrent remote `style bold=true` against a local `removeStyle bold` differently from set-vs-set LWW, a peer's stale bold can survive/resurrect after the local toggle-off. The concurrency suite (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts) only exercises set-vs-set style ops (lines 220-365); no case covers remove-vs-set.

samples.summary: The named-style exception writes a permanent dead `false` that survives a later block-type change, recreating the hazard the change exists to remove
samples.evidence: `if (defaults[key]) continue;` keeps `italic: false` on runs inside a Heading 6. If the block is later converted to a paragraph (or Heading 6 is redefined without italic), the run keeps a `false` that no longer overrides anything: it renders identically to a neighbour lacking the key, but `inlineStylesEqual` (types.ts:406-407) can never merge them, and no code path ever rewrites it back to `undefined`. That is the same dead-flag/lazy-cascade hazard the doc comment at lines 387-392 describes, now created deliberately with no cleanup on `setBlockType` or on style redefinition (`rematerializeDocSpacing` only touches block spacing, named-styles.ts:163).

samples.summary: `styleOffAsClear` calls `findBlock` once per visited block slice, adding a potentially full recursive cell walk to every toggle-off over a large cell rectangle
samples.evidence: `applyInlineStyleToCells` visits every block of every cell (range-slices.ts:60-66) and now calls `styleOffAsClear` → `this.findBlock(blockId)` per block. When the parent map is stale (fresh blocks since last layout) `findBlockInCells` falls back to `walkCellsForBlock` over body + header + footer (document.ts:214-221), making a bold-off over a large table O(cells × document). Correct, just quadratic on the hottest editing path; the block's named style could be resolved once per cell/table instead.

finding.summary: Yorkie tree write ignores the superscript/subscript mutual exclusion that the cache write applies, so the CRDT keeps both flags while the local cache shows one
finding.evidence: `applyStyle` (line 1707) updates the cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper(block, from, to, style)`, and that helper (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:337-343) resolves `{superscript:true}` into `{superscript:true, subscript:undefined}` and, via `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325), *deletes* `subscript` from the run. The tree path (`applyStyleInTree`, line 1716) is handed the RAW `style`: `serializeInlineStyle(style)` at line 1882 emits only `superscript:'true'` and `removedInlineStyleAttrs(style)` at line 1883 returns `[]` because `subscript` is not a key of the patch. Since `styleByPath` only merges, the pre-existing `subscript='true'` attribute survives on the Tree node. Ctrl+. on subscripted text (text-editor.ts:899) therefore leaves the CRDT with both `superscript` and `subscript` set; `parseInlineStyle` (line 168-173) reads both back on reload or on any remote-driven cache invalidation, so the run silently changes appearance/state relative to what the user saw. This is exactly the 'styleByPath cannot delete' class of bug the surrounding comment block (lines 1871-1881) claims is handled on this path.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. `applyStyle` splits its two writes: the cache write goes through `applyInlineStyleHelper` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:331-343), which resolves `{superscript:true}` into `{superscript:true, subscript:undefined}` and, via `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325), deletes `subscript` from the run. The CRDT write (`applyStyleInTree`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1716, 1882-1889) receives the RAW patch: `serializeInlineStyle` (:106-134) emits only `superscript:'true'`, and `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (:144-163) returns `[]` because it requires `key in style && style[key] === undefined` and `subscript` is not a key of the patch. `styleByPath` is called as a pure merge (`{...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs}`), so a pre-existing `subscript='true'` attribute survives on the Tree node while the cache no longer has it. The path is live: text-editor.ts:899 (`Ctrl/Cmd+.`) → `toggleStyle` (:2858-2903, which never injects the counterpart key) → `applyStyleToSelection` → `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:375-378) → `styleOffAsClear` (:399-418, only rewrites keys explicitly set to `false`) → `store.applyStyle` with `{superscript:true}`. No read-side normalization exists: `parseInlineStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:172-173) and `treeNodeToInline` (:349-363) materialize both flags on reload/remote refresh, and consumers read them raw (paint-layout.ts:378-379, 411-413; export/docx-style-map.ts:79-80 would emit two conflicting `w:vertAlign` elements). The invariant is deliberate and tested at the model layer (packages/docs/test/model/document.test.ts:616-645), so the CRDT silently violates an invariant the rest of the stack assumes — a broken-invariant / persisted-state-divergence bug in the correctness lane, at exactly the location the surrounding comment (:1871-1881) claims is handled.

finding.summary: Every style write, including the now-hot pure-clear toggle-off, re-asserts the node's full existing attribute map, which can clobber a concurrent remote attribute change
finding.evidence: `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })` re-sends every attribute already on the node even when `styleAttrs` is empty (the pure-clear case `{bold: undefined}` that, per the comment added at lines 1873-1875, is now every B/I/U/S toggle-off). The comment two lines above states styleByPath 'only merges', so passing `existingAttrs` is unnecessary; because it is sent with a fresh local timestamp, an LWW-per-attribute Tree resolves it over a concurrent peer's change to an unrelated attribute (e.g. peer sets `color` while this client toggles bold off), reverting the peer's edit. The delta puts this redundant full-attribute rewrite on the hottest editing path.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim: yorkie-doc-store.ts:1885-1886 spreads the node's full existing attribute map into every styleByPath call (`{ ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs }`), and the comment at :1871-1875 confirms both that styleByPath 'only merges' (making existingAttrs redundant) and that since issue #749 every B/I/U/S toggle-off is a pure-clear, i.e. this sits on the hottest editing path where styleAttrs from serializeInlineStyle (:106-134) can be empty and the sole payload is a re-assertion of pre-existing attributes with a fresh local timestamp. No guard makes it unreachable: applyStyle (:1697-1723) and applyStyles (:1733-1775) both route all inline-style writes through applyStyleInTree, and real toolbar toggles call them (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:393-403, text-format-group.tsx:100-119). The repo's own note that native split copies attributes verbatim (docs/tasks/archive/2026/04/20260413-yorkie-native-split-merge-lessons.md:7) undercuts any 'needed to restore attributes after split' defense. I could not disprove the LWW-per-attribute clobber mechanism because @yorkie-js/sdk@0.7.16 (packages/frontend/package.json:93) is not installed in this tree, so the RHT set semantics were unverifiable. Losing a peer's concurrent attribute edit is data overwrite, which is in the correctness lane; uncertainty keeps the finding.
